summary: 36 declaration-sized planning nodes across R.1-R.7, including both reserved exports. Explicit Tate-coordinate normalization, independent rational rank/lattice paths, historical pi factor, corrected source provenance, and an unresolved early-Deligne producer cycle. No stage or implementation is claimed complete.

nodes.title: Arithmetic special-linear levels
nodes.statement: For a number field F and N>=2, construct Gamma_N=SL_N(O_F) as an arithmetic subgroup of Res_{F/Q} SL_N, its block inclusions, and X_N=G_N(R)/K_N for a specified maximal compact K_N. The construction contains no finiteness or comparison theorem as an assumed field.
hypotheses: F is a finite extension of Q; O_F is its full ring of integers.
Use real Lie groups, and include the component action of K_N.
proofSteps: Use the integral model and all archimedean embeddings to construct the discrete embedding.
Take the symmetric-space quotient and the block maps; transport choices by actual quotient maps.
Request arithmeticity/reduction and quotient foundations from AA.3 and ALS.2. General division-algebra orders are a separate remaining extension (G4), not silently replaced by this case.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Finite rational Betti numbers at each level
nodes.statement: For F a number field, N>=2 and q>=0, H^q(Gamma_N,Q) is finite-dimensional.
hypotheses: Ordinary group cohomology with trivial Q coefficients, not compactly supported or L2 cohomology.
proofSteps: Choose a normal torsion-free subgroup Gamma' of finite index using the supplied arithmetic theorem.
Use its finite CW-type Borel--Serre model, with finite many cells in each degree, to get finite-dimensional rational cohomology.
Use restriction and averaging, or the finite-quotient Hochschild--Serre argument over Q, to identify H^q(Gamma_N,Q) with invariants. This does not prove finite generation of K-groups.
acceptance: Do not replace Gamma_N by a torsion-free group without the finite-index comparison.

nodes.title: Invariant-form comparison at an arithmetic level
nodes.statement: Construct j_N^q:H_cts^q(G_N(R),R)->H^q(Gamma_N,R), identified under van Est with descent of invariant forms on X_N; it is natural for the specified block maps.
hypotheses: q>=0; trivial finite-dimensional real coefficients.
Use full maximal compact groups and the finite component action.
proofSteps: AF.1a supplies smoothing and van Est, not the arithmetic comparison.
For a torsion-free level descend invariant forms to Gamma'\X_N and apply de Rham/group-cohomology comparison from ALS.5.
Descend from Gamma' to Gamma_N by rational/real averaging and prove independence using a common normal finite-index subgroup. Cup and block compatibility must come from maps of complexes (G1).
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Special-linear homology model for higher K-theory
nodes.statement: For O_F construct a connected homotopy-associative, homotopy-commutative H-space of CW type Y_F, compatible identifications pi_q(Y_F)=K_q(O_F) for q>=2 and H_*(Y_F,Q)=colim_N H_*(SL_N(O_F),Q), preserving block-sum Hopf structures.
hypotheses: F is a number field.
All homotopy comparisons are pointed and natural up to the specified homotopies.
proofSteps: Start from the actual plus/group-completion model supplied by K.2:plus.
Prove the special-linear/determinant or suitable-cover comparison, including the required stable elementary-group and K_1 identification, before replacing general-linear homology.
Transport block sum, Hurewicz and rational homology through these comparisons. G2 records that this model-level bridge is not decomposed here; an arbitrary group isomorphism does not suffice.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

sources.match: This is the model-level input used to pass from stable special-linear cohomology to higher K-groups.

nodes.title: Dimensions of stable cohomological indecomposables
nodes.statement: Let A_F=lim_N H^*(SL_N(O_F),R), in the degreewise eventually stable sense, and Q^q(A_F)=A_F^q/(A_F^{>0} A_F^{>0})^q. For q>=2 its dimension is 0 for even q, r_2(F) for q=3 mod 4, and r_1(F)+r_2(F) for q=1 mod 4.
hypotheses: The inverse-system stabilization and the multiplication/Hopf structure must first be constructed.
r_1 counts real embeddings; r_2 counts conjugate pairs of nonreal embeddings.
proofSteps: Use j_N and compute compact-dual cohomology degree by degree.
Extract primitive generators, not every cohomology class; a decomposable product contributes no indecomposable.
For every q choose a level satisfying the analytic comparison and compact-dual restriction ranges simultaneously. Keep these ranges separate; G3 requests their explicit functions and proofs.
Obtain finite-dimensional stabilized indecomposables. No finite-generation theorem for K_q is used.
acceptance: Reproduce q=2,3,5: 0,r_2,r_1+r_2. Do not infer a universal numerical stability bound from a single family.

api.name: BorelRegulators.stableIndecomposables

sources.match: The stable comparison and final periodic formula are checked; the full compact-dual table and analytic interiors still need decomposition.

nodes.title: Rational Hurewicz lands in primitive homology
nodes.statement: For a connected homotopy-commutative H-space Y of finite rational Betti type in the range in question, rational Hurewicz identifies pi_q(Y) tensor Q with P H_q(Y,Q); duality identifies this with the dual of cohomological indecomposables.
hypotheses: q>=2; Y has CW type, homotopy-associative and homotopy-commutative multiplication, and the nilpotent/simple-space hypotheses needed for rationalization.
P denotes primitives for the diagonal coproduct, not all homology.
proofSteps: Apply the rational H-space theorem with its precise finite-type hypotheses.
Identify primitive homology as the annihilator of products of positive-degree cohomology classes using the finite-dimensional pairing.
Extend scalars Q->R compatibly. H.6 is requested for rationalization; the rational H-space theorem itself needs a named producer or an explicit extension (G2).
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

api.name: BorelRegulators.primitiveHurewicz

sources.match: This passage explains primitives and indecomposables; finite-level Betti bounds alone do not establish the stable hypotheses.

nodes.title: Borel rank theorem for rings of integers
nodes.statement: For every number field F and integer n>=2, dim_Q(K_{2n-1}(O_F) tensor_Z Q)=d_n(F), where d_n=r_1+r_2 for odd n and d_n=r_2 for even n.
hypotheses: K denotes Quillen K-theory, with its K.2:plus comparison.
No finite-generation hypothesis on K_{2n-1}(O_F) is assumed.
proofSteps: Use the special-linear K-model and rational primitive Hurewicz.
Apply the indecomposable dimension theorem in q=2n-1.
If n is odd then q=1 mod 4; if n is even then q=3 mod 4. Scalar extension preserves the finite dimension.
acceptance: Preserve this reserved ID. No dependency on ArithmeticKTheory:N.3:ranks or on finite generation.

api.name: BorelRegulators.borelRankTheorem

sources.match: The checked theorem covers orders in central division algebras; this reserved export is its full-ring-of-integers specialization.

nodes.title: Real Tate coefficient line with fixed generator
nodes.statement: For j>=0 set tau_j=(2*pi*i)^j and L_j=tau_j R subset C. Treat L_j as a one-dimensional real vector space with the displayed generator, not as a complex vector space.
hypotheses: The embeddings of R and Q into C are fixed.
proofSteps: Construct the real-linear map a |-> tau_j*a; tau_j is nonzero.
Define its inverse on the image by division by tau_j followed by the real-part map.
Retain this generator in every coordinate conversion. Replacing tau_j by i^j changes a covolume by a nonrational factor in general.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Projection of a complex quotient to the complementary real line
nodes.statement: For n>=1, pi_{n-1}(z)=(z+(-1)^{n-1} conjugate(z))/2 induces a real-linear equivalence C/L_n -> L_{n-1}.
hypotheses: The quotient is of real additive/vector spaces, not a quotient of complex vector spaces.
proofSteps: The formula is the eigenspace projection for conjugation with eigenvalue (-1)^{n-1}.
Its kernel is L_n and its image is L_{n-1}; the two lines have complementary parities.
Apply quotient descent and use inclusion of L_{n-1} followed by the quotient map as inverse.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Intrinsic real target of the higher regulator
nodes.statement: For E_F=Hom(F,C), c(sigma)=conjugation composed with sigma and epsilon_n=(-1)^{n-1}, define V_n(F)={a:E_F->R | a(c(sigma))=epsilon_n*a(sigma)}. Define d_n as in the rank theorem.
hypotheses: F is a number field; n>=2.
proofSteps: Take the kernel of the real-linear operator a |-> (a(c(sigma))-epsilon_n*a(sigma))_sigma.
Relate orbits of c to infinite places; pinned InfinitePlace supplies the place carrier, not yet all counting lemmas.
At fixed embeddings the condition is unrestricted for odd n and forces zero for even n. The finite embedding/counting API still needs a pinned audit (G5).
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Coordinates from conjugate-pair representatives
nodes.statement: Choose an ordering of real embeddings and one embedding from each nonreal conjugate pair. Evaluation gives a real-linear equivalence V_n(F) -> R^{I_n}, where I_n is the complex-pair index set plus the real-embedding index set exactly when n is odd.
hypotheses: Finite exhaustive orbit representatives, with disjointness and no duplicate pairs.
Coordinate Lebesgue measure is used; it is not the Euclidean subspace measure inherited from R^{E_F}.
proofSteps: Evaluate on the chosen embeddings.
Extend inversely by epsilon_n on the omitted conjugates and by zero on real embeddings when n is even.
Check both composites pointwise. A changed representative contributes a sign; a reordering contributes a permutation.
acceptance: Do not introduce a factor sqrt(2) by switching to inherited ambient Euclidean volume.

nodes.title: The compact-dual transport fixing the Borel normalization
nodes.statement: For G=GL_N(C) as a real Lie group, K=U(N), q=2n-1, construct the chain from H^q(G,L_n) through H^q(K,L_n), H^q((U(N)xU(N))/U(N)_diag,L_n), relative Lie algebra cohomology and multiplication by i^q on tangent arguments, to H_cts^q(G,L_{n-1}).
hypotheses: n>=2, N>=n; trivial coefficient action.
The diagonal compact subgroup and the order of the two compact factors are fixed as in Tamme p.69.
proofSteps: Use the deformation retraction and the compact-dual identification in the displayed source chain.
Transport invariant alternating forms on i*p to forms on p, tracking multiplication by i^{2n-1}; use the real coefficient-line identification, not a silent scalar extension.
Apply van Est. G1 includes the homogeneous de Rham and orientation/sign checks required by this chain.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Normalized continuous Borel class
nodes.statement: For n>=2 and N>=n, define b_{n,N} in H_cts^{2n-1}(GL_N(C),L_{n-1}) as the image of the universal topological Chern-character component Ch_n^top(E_univ) in H^{2n}(BGL_N(C),L_n), under cohomological suspension and compact-dual transport. Use the Chern-character component, not the Chern class c_n.
hypotheses: Fix the standard positive generator tau_j of each Tate line as above.
Topological Chern character and suspension with the source convention are requested, not claimed to exist at baseline.
proofSteps: Construct the universal Chern-character class, then its suspension.
Apply compact-dual transport and retain its restriction to the discrete group.

Normalization test: its image in absolute Lie cohomology is represented by -2*(n-1)!/(2n-1)! times pi_{n-1} Tr((g^{-1}dg)^{2n-1}); wedge/matrix multiplication are retained. G6 records unexpanded Chern-character and suspension foundations.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Complex conjugation on the normalized class
nodes.statement: Conjugation on GL_N(C) pulls b_{n,N} back to (-1)^{n-1} b_{n,N}, when the coefficient line is expressed using the fixed tau_{n-1}.
hypotheses: n>=2; use the same coefficient and compact-dual conventions as continuous-borel-class.
proofSteps: Track conjugation on the Chern-character and compact-dual maps.
Check the sign against the projection/form formula in Lemma 3.20.
Do not deduce equality of relative classes merely from equality of absolute images without a justified injectivity statement; G6 includes that check or a direct naturality proof.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Primitivity under block sum
nodes.statement: For block sum mu:GL_A(C)xGL_B(C)->GL_{A+B}(C), mu^* b_{n,A+B}=pr_1^* b_{n,A}+pr_2^* b_{n,B} in the stable range.
hypotheses: A,B are in the range where the classes and stabilization maps are defined.
The same universal Chern-character convention is used at every rank.
proofSteps: Use additivity of Ch_n on direct sums.
Commute suspension, compact-dual transport and restriction with block maps.
Thus the class is primitive; prove stabilization compatibility by adding a trivial block. The trace of a block-diagonal matrix provides an independent local check.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

api.name: BorelRegulators.borelClassBlockSum

sources.match: The source construction motivates this separately named compatibility lemma; its map-level proof is a remaining part of G6.

nodes.title: Normalized higher Borel regulator
nodes.statement: For a number field F and n>=2 define rho^B_{F,n}:K_{2n-1}(O_F)->V_n(F) by rho^B(x)(sigma)=tau_{n-1}^{-1}<b_n,h(K(sigma|O_F)(x))>. Compose with target-coordinates to obtain the reserved export K_{2n-1}(O_F)->R^{d_n(F)}. The quotient is real because the pairing lies in L_{n-1}.
hypotheses: K(sigma|O_F):K_{2n-1}(O_F)->K_{2n-1}(C) is the covariant map of rings.
Use ordinary integral Hurewicz for the evaluation; rational Hurewicz is not needed to define the map.
proofSteps: Map to complex K-theory at every embedding and evaluate the stabilized discrete class on Hurewicz.
Use conjugation to land in V_n(F), and additivity/primitivity to obtain an additive map.
Extend uniquely to a real-linear map K_{2n-1}(O_F) tensor_Z R -> V_n(F). This definition assumes no rank or finite generation.
acceptance: Preserve this reserved ID. No invocation of the rank theorem in the definition. The selected Tate generator is part of the public normalization.

nodes.title: Nondegeneracy of the regulator pairing
nodes.statement: The map rho^B_{F,n} tensor R is a real-linear isomorphism onto V_n(F), for every number field F and n>=2.
hypotheses: The normalized classes must be identified with a basis of stable indecomposables, not merely shown to be nonzero somewhere.
proofSteps: Identify the normalized embedding classes with the real/complex compact-dual primitive generators, including their nonzero constants.
Dualize the resulting basis using primitive Hurewicz.
Use target-coordinates and compare the actual pairing matrix. Equal source and target dimensions alone do not prove this theorem. G7 is the unresolved basis/nondegeneracy comparison.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

sources.match: Stable cohomology supplies the route, but the normalized basis comparison remains a distinct proof obligation.

nodes.title: The image is a full lattice, with torsion kernel
nodes.statement: For F a number field and n>=2, rho^B has kernel equal to torsion in K_{2n-1}(O_F), and its image is a full lattice in V_n(F).
hypotheses: Use the independent finite generation of K_{2n-1}(O_F), and regulator-real-isomorphism.
proofSteps: Write the finitely generated abelian group modulo torsion as Z^d.
A class mapped to zero vanishes after tensoring with R, hence is torsion; torsion maps to zero in a real vector space.
The real extension is invertible, so the image of a Z-basis is an R-basis and its integer span is discrete and cocompact.
acceptance: A full-rank map from a non-finitely-generated group need not have discrete image; test the failure with Z[1/2] in R.

api.name: BorelRegulators.regulatorLattice
api.statement: For F a number field and n>=2, rho^B has kernel equal to torsion in K_{2n-1}(O_F), and its image is a full lattice in V_n(F).

sources.match: Finiteness is needed here, not upstream in the rational rank proof.

nodes.title: Regulator covolume in coordinate measure
nodes.statement: Choose a Z-basis of K_{2n-1}(O_F)/torsion and target coordinates. Define R^B_n(F)=abs(det M), where the columns of M are their regulator images. For dimension zero set det(empty)=1.
hypotheses: Use regulator-lattice; the coordinate measure assigns volume 1 to the unit cube in R^{I_n}.
proofSteps: Construct the free quotient basis and evaluate the regulator on representatives.
Torsion-kernel ensures representative independence.
Use the determinant definition with the empty-index convention. Choice independence is not part of the definition and is proved next.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Independence of bases and embedding representatives
nodes.statement: R^B_n(F) is unchanged by replacing the integral basis, ordering embeddings, or replacing a nonreal representative by its conjugate.
hypotheses: The Tate generator tau_{n-1} and coordinate-measure convention are held fixed.
proofSteps: Integral change of basis multiplies M on the right by U in GL_d(Z), with determinant +/-1.
Target changes multiply M on the left by a signed permutation matrix.
Take absolute determinants. This proves independence of the indicated choices, not invariance under arbitrary rescaling of the Tate line.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Effect of multiplying a regulator by a scalar
nodes.statement: If two maps from the same free abelian group of rank d to the same measured real vector space satisfy f=c*g, with c a nonzero real number, their determinant covolumes satisfy R(f)=abs(c)^d R(g), including d=0.
hypotheses: Identical integral lattice, coordinate space and measure for both maps.
proofSteps: In compatible bases M_f=c M_g.
Use determinant homogeneity and absolute values; the empty determinant gives 1 on both sides.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Leading coefficient of the continued Dedekind zeta function
nodes.statement: For n>=2 let zeta_F^mer be the meromorphic continuation of the ideal Dirichlet series and s0=1-n. Once its zero order d_n is proved, define zeta_F^*(s0) as the unique nonzero coefficient a with zeta_F^mer(s)=(s-s0)^d_n(a+O(s-s0)).
hypotheses: Continuation agrees with the pinned NumberField.dedekindZeta on Re(s)>1.
Use germs or analytic factorization, not the raw LSeries value outside convergence.
proofSteps: Request the continued function and its agreement theorem from AL.1.
Construct the normalized germ by dividing by the exact zero power and extending holomorphically.
Evaluate this germ at s0; uniqueness is by identity of analytic germs. Existence and nonvanishing are supplied by the next theorem, not assumed in the continued-function definition.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Exact order at the negative integer
nodes.statement: For a number field F and n>=2, zeta_F^mer is holomorphic at 1-n, its zero order is d_n(F), and its leading coefficient there is nonzero.
hypotheses: Gamma_R(s)=pi^{-s/2} Gamma(s/2), Gamma_C(s)=2(2*pi)^{-s} Gamma(s).
Lambda_F(s)=|D_F|^{s/2} Gamma_R(s)^{r_1} Gamma_C(s)^{r_2} zeta_F^mer(s) satisfies Lambda_F(s)=Lambda_F(1-s).
proofSteps: At n>1 the Euler product is positive and nonzero and all completed factors are finite and nonzero.
At 1-n, Gamma_C has a simple pole at each complex place; Gamma_R has a simple pole exactly when n is odd.
Factor the gamma functions into their exact pole powers and nonzero holomorphic units. The functional equation makes the completed germ a unit, forcing a zero of exactly d_n, not just at least d_n.
acceptance: For totally real F and n=2, the zero order is 0: 1-n=-1 is neither a pole nor a forced zero.

api.name: BorelRegulators.zetaZeroOrder
api.statement: For a number field F and n>=2, zeta_F^mer is holomorphic at 1-n, its zero order is d_n(F), and its leading coefficient there is nonzero.

nodes.title: Borel's historical determinant-line regulator
nodes.statement: For m>=1, define R_m^{77}(F)>0 by the determinant-line comparison j^*(x_m)=R_m^{77}(F)*y_m, where x_m and y_m generate the dual exterior powers of the integral images in pi_{2m+1}(X_u) tensor Q and K_{2m+1}(O_F) tensor Q respectively, as in Borel 6.4.
hypotheses: Use the compact-dual stable model X_u, its homotopy lattice, and the comparison j.
m=n-1 in our weight convention; determinant degree is d_n(F).
proofSteps: Construct the two integral images in their rational vector spaces, then their top exterior powers and dual lattices.
Use the nondegenerate comparison and choose signs to make the scalar positive.
Keep this regulator separate from R^B_n(F): no rational equality or missing pi factor is built into a definition. The compact-dual integral lattice and its comparison are part of G8.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

api.statement: The positive determinant-line scalar R_m^{77}(F).

api.name: BorelRegulators.compactDualDeterminantLattice

nodes.title: Rational proportionality with the historical normalization
nodes.statement: For F a number field and n>=2, zeta_F^*(1-n)/(pi^{d_n(F)}*R_{n-1}^{77}(F)) is a nonzero rational number, viewed in C.
hypotheses: Historical regulator means precisely borel77-determinant.
Use the corrected discriminant conventions of the 1980 erratum in the proof of the 1977 result.
proofSteps: Read Borel 6.2 and 6.4 together: the rational determinant comparison is followed by the functional-equation conversion.
Track m=n-1, the degree d=[F:Q] and d_n separately.
The original proof needs the compact cycles, nonzero primitive restrictions, finite-place volumes and archimedean determinant factors; these are G8-G9, not discharged by citing the last formula.
Do not substitute R^B_n(F) for R_{n-1}^{77}(F) until the missing normalization conversion is proved. No integral Lichtenbaum equality or dyadic factor is asserted.
acceptance: Never advertise zeta_F^*(1-n)/R^B_n(F) as rational solely on the basis of this node.

api.name: BorelRegulators.borel77LeadingTerm
api.statement: For F a number field and n>=2, zeta_F^*(1-n)/(pi^{d_n(F)}*R_{n-1}^{77}(F)) is a nonzero rational number, viewed in C.

The erratum replaces absolute discriminant by the discriminant in specified rational forms and removes specified powers of i.

nodes.title: Unramified special-linear local volume factor
nodes.statement: Let O be a nonarchimedean local ring of integers with residue field of cardinality q and r>=2. For the smooth SL_r/O model, the gauge measure normalized by O-additive volume 1 gives volume(SL_r(O))=prod_{j=2}^r(1-q^{-j}).
hypotheses: Use the integral invariant gauge form and smooth reduction fibers of dimension r^2-1.
This is a local coordinate normalization, not yet the global discriminant-normalized Tamagawa measure.
proofSteps: Each reduction fiber has measure q^{-(r^2-1)} under the specified smooth-model measure.
Count GL_r(F_q) by successive independent columns and divide by q-1 using the surjective determinant map.
Divide |SL_r(F_q)| by q^{r^2-1}. Non-split or ramified models require different local input, not this formula.
acceptance: For r=2 the answer is 1-q^{-2}; normalized compact-open probability measure instead has volume 1.

api.name: BorelRegulators.splitLocalVolumeFactor
api.statement: Let O be a nonarchimedean local ring of integers with residue field of cardinality q and r>=2. For the smooth SL_r/O model, the gauge measure normalized by O-additive volume 1 gives volume(SL_r(O))=prod_{j=2}^r(1-q^{-j}).

sources.match: The split local factor is isolated here; the smooth-measure theorem and global conversion remain requests/gaps.

nodes.title: Convergence and evaluation of the split finite-place product
nodes.statement: For a number field F and r>=2, prod_{v finite} prod_{j=2}^r(1-Nv^{-j}) converges absolutely to prod_{j=2}^r zeta_F(j)^{-1}, a positive nonzero real number.
hypotheses: Use the convergent ideal Euler products at integers j>=2.
Local factors are those of split-local-volume-factor; no assertion about a full adelic quotient volume is made.
proofSteps: Use absolute convergence for each of the finitely many exponents j.
Interchange a finite product with the convergent place product.
Removing finitely many places inserts precisely the inverse of the removed finite product; each such factor is nonzero.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

api.name: BorelRegulators.finiteEulerVolumeProduct
api.statement: For a number field F and r>=2, prod_{v finite} prod_{j=2}^r(1-Nv^{-j}) converges absolutely to prod_{j=2}^r zeta_F(j)^{-1}, a positive nonzero real number.

sources.match: The local-to-Euler-product portion can be separated from compact cycles and Tamagawa rationality.

nodes.title: Beilinson regulator in the identical target coordinates
nodes.statement: Let r^Beil_{F,n}:K_{2n-1}(O_F)->V_n(F) be the embeddingwise Beilinson regulator to H_D^1(Spec C,R(n))=C/L_n, followed by tate-quotient-projection and division by the same tau_{n-1}.
hypotheses: n>=2; use the universal Chern-character component, not c_n.

The independent Deligne/universal-class construction must be supplied before the comparison. M.6 supplies motivic weights, not this construction; the construction-only part of M.8 needs an early export independent of R.7 (G10).
proofSteps: Use the construction-only Deligne/universal Chern-character regulator at every embedding. Do not import the whole M.8 stage, since its analytic comparison depends on R.7.
Identify the Deligne group as a real quotient with its actual map, then use the explicit projection.
Check conjugation descent using the Deligne real structure. G10 records the unresolved early-producer split; no theorem equating this map to Borel is used in its construction.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Exact Borel--Beilinson factor for these classes
nodes.statement: For F a number field and n>=2, rho^B_{F,n}=2*r^Beil_{F,n}, with both maps valued in V_n(F) and using the identical Tate-coordinate conversion.
hypotheses: Universal Chern-character, suspension, Hurewicz and Deligne sign conventions are exactly those of Tamme 3.6.
proofSteps: First compare the universal continuous/discrete Borel class with the universal Beilinson class for C, after the explicit real quotient projection.
Follow Tamme 3.21 through relative K-theory, odd topological K-vanishing, the relative Chern-character comparison and the two cocycle descriptions.
The coefficients of those cocycles differ by 2. Proof interiors of 3.11, 3.16 and 3.18 and the required surjectivity are explicit G10, not claimed checked.
Evaluate on Hurewicz and apply the ring maps at every embedding, then the identical real-linear coordinate map.

nodes.title: Restriction and trace on intrinsic targets
nodes.statement: For a finite extension L/F of number fields define P:V_n(F)->V_n(L) by (Pa)(tau)=a(tau|F), and T:V_n(L)->V_n(F) by (Tb)(sigma)=sum_{tau|F=sigma} b(tau).
hypotheses: n>=2; every embedding F->C extends in [L:F] ways since L/F is separable.
proofSteps: Check that restriction of embeddings commutes with complex conjugation.
Conjugation permutes each extension fiber onto the conjugate fiber, so the sums satisfy the required parity.
Bundle the resulting real-linear maps. There is no ad hoc factor 1/2 on complex pairs.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Trace after restriction is multiplication by degree
nodes.statement: T composed with P equals [L:F] times the identity on V_n(F).
hypotheses: Finite extension L/F of number fields; target maps as defined above.
proofSteps: For each sigma, all summands equal a(sigma).
Count the extension fiber using separability, and apply function extensionality.
For a real embedding in even weight, conjugate nonreal extensions cancel in the trace of an arbitrary target vector; this does not change T P.
acceptance: Check the stated carrier, hypotheses and all comparison maps; this is a plan, not an implemented declaration.

nodes.title: Regulator compatibility with scalar extension and transfer
nodes.statement: For O_F->O_L and n>=2, rho_L^B composed with res=P composed with rho_F^B, and rho_F^B composed with tr=T composed with rho_L^B, where tr is restriction-of-scalars transfer on finite projective modules.

All fields and embedding fibers are as in embedding-restriction-and-trace.
proofSteps: Restriction follows by functoriality of ring maps and Hurewicz.
For transfer, base-change the restricted module to C and decompose it as the direct sum indexed by extensions of an embedding.
Use the transfer/base-change map comparison from K.7 and block primitivity; equality of dimensions or ranks is insufficient.

nodes.title: Totally real even-weight zero-dimensional test
nodes.statement: For totally real F and even n>=2, V_n(F)=0, both regulator maps are zero, both determinant covolumes are 1, and the continued zeta function has zero order 0 at 1-n.
hypotheses: The lattice and analytic conclusions require their corresponding nodes, not just the target definition.
proofSteps: There are only real embeddings and epsilon_n=-1, so every target value is zero.
Use the rank/lattice theorems for the free K-quotient and the empty determinant convention.
Apply the gamma-factor zero-order result; there is no pole at -1 when n=2.

nodes.title: Imaginary-quadratic orientation and factor test
nodes.statement: For imaginary quadratic F and n=2, V_2(F) consists of (a,-a), hence is one-dimensional. Changing the chosen embedding negates the scalar regulator and preserves its covolume; the Borel--Beilinson determinant factor is 2.
hypotheses: There is exactly one conjugate pair and no real embeddings.
proofSteps: Write the two target coordinates and apply the parity condition.
Use representative independence of the absolute determinant.
Specialize the determinant comparison to d_2=1. This does not identify either map with the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm; its exact comparison constant remains G11/P.2.
